name: TOPdesk
description: TOPdesk ITSM: incidents, changes, assets, operators, persons and branches, with TOPdesk's FIQL query language for precise filtering. REST API, Basic auth with an application password.
instructions:
**Use an application password, never the operator's own.**
1. In TOPdesk open **Modules → Supporting Files → Operator Management**, pick the operator the integration should act as, and on its card create an **Application Password**. TOPdesk shows it once.
2. Give that operator exactly the permission groups the agent needs — TOPdesk enforces them per module, and a missing one produces a 403 rather than an empty list, which is at least honest.
3. Set `TOPDESK_URL` to your instance root (e.g. `https://mycompany.topdesk.net`, no trailing slash), `TOPDESK_USERNAME` to the operator login name and `TOPDESK_APP_PASSWORD` to the generated value.

**FIQL is the query language, and it is worth learning.** `query=status==firstLine;caller.branch.name==Berlin` filters server-side. `;` is AND, `,` is OR, `==` is equals, `=lt=`/`=gt=` compare, `=in=` takes a list. The tools below pass a `query` string through verbatim.

**Paging** is `start` and `page_size` (max 100 on most endpoints), not page numbers. TOPdesk returns 206 Partial Content when more rows exist and 204 No Content when the result is empty — a 204 with no body is a successful search that matched nothing.

**`fields` cuts the response down.** Incident records are large; `fields=id,number,briefDescription,status,caller.dynamicName` keeps the answer readable.

**Writes**: `topdesk_create_incident` opens a real incident, which notifies whoever the process assigns it to.

tools.name: topdesk_get_version
tools.description: Read the TOPdesk version this instance runs. No parameters and no module permission needed — the fastest proof that URL and application password are right.

tools.name: topdesk_list_incidents
tools.description: List incidents with FIQL filtering. `query=status==firstLine;closed==false` is the common 'what is open' shape; name the fields you want to keep the answer readable.

query.description: FIQL query, e.g. status==firstLine;closed==false. `;` is AND, `,` is OR.

fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. id,number,briefDescription,status.

tools.name: topdesk_get_incident
tools.description: Read one incident by its TOPdesk number or UUID, with its caller, category, status, operator group, SLA target dates and request text.

number.description: Incident number (e.g. I 2609 123) or the incident UUID.

tools.name: topdesk_get_incident_progress
tools.description: Read the progress trail of one incident: every action and memo in order, with author, timestamp and whether it is invisible to the caller.

tools.name: topdesk_list_changes
tools.description: List change activities with their number, requester, status, planned dates and change type. The change-management side of TOPdesk.

tools.name: topdesk_list_persons
tools.description: List persons (the callers incidents are raised for) with their name, e-mail, branch and department. Filter with FIQL to find one before raising an incident.

tools.name: topdesk_list_operators
tools.description: List operators (the staff who work the queue) with their name, e-mail and the operator groups they belong to.

tools.name: topdesk_list_branches
tools.description: List branches — the sites or client organisations TOPdesk groups people and assets under — with their name, address and client reference number.

tools.name: topdesk_search_assets
tools.description: Search the asset management module for configuration items by name or type, returning their id, name, template and status.

searchTerm.description: Fragment matched against the asset name.

templateName.description: Restrict to one asset template, e.g. Laptop.

tools.name: topdesk_create_incident
tools.description: Open a real incident in the live instance. TOPdesk routes and notifies it according to the process configuration, so this is not a dry run.

callerId.description: UUID of the person the incident is raised for, from topdesk_list_persons.

request.description: Full request text. HTML is accepted.

operatorGroupId.description: UUID of the operator group to route the incident to.

categoryName.description: Category name, as configured in this instance.

entryTypeName.description: Entry type name, e.g. Telefoon, E-mail, Self Service Desk.
